contributions.statement: Do not treat a developer's approval of agent-applied edits as knowledge transfer: agent users recalled markedly less of their own code than chatbot-snippet users even after controlling for task accuracy, so require an owner walkthrough or explanation for agent-written code they must maintain.
contributions.evidence: §4.1/§4.3 Figs. 1, 4, 6: comprehension much lower for agent group (p<0.002, d>0.80) with regression controlling for initial accuracy; audit narrows it to recall of names/snippets/purpose (App. A.9.2), with no difference on behavioural questions. 54 students, toy HTML/JS game.
relative_to: AI assistance reduces skill formation / code comprehension (known pre-2026 user studies)

contributions.statement: Pasting acceptance criteria verbatim into the agent and auto-accepting its edits was associated with the lowest comprehension; translating criteria into concrete technical instructions and reviewing per file was associated with more.
contributions.evidence: §5.1 prompt-strategy table (copy criteria 0.654 vs translated 0.743) and Table 2 (auto-accept vs per-file review); correlational, cells of 5-25 users, background ability confounded (audit).

reason: The agent-vs-snippet comprehension gap is a controlled, moderate result that refines the known deskilling finding to agentic editing; the spec-pasting result is only a hypothesis.
